receipt.public_excerpt: achieving a 38.1% success rate on OSWorld for full computer use tasks, and 58.1% on WebArena and 87% on WebVoyager for web-based tasks.

evidence_items.explanation: Operator is a web agent, and on the two web benchmarks it succeeded on most tasks (58% and 87%). That cuts against "rarely completes." Only the full-computer benchmark is below half. These figures are vendor-reported.

receipt.public_excerpt: However, it still makes too many mistakes for human users to rely on it for important tasks without constant supervision.

evidence_items.explanation: Early testers found Operator slow and error-prone. This supports the general thrust of the Operator criticism, though not the claim that it rarely succeeds.

receipt.public_excerpt: Peculiar source selection: The system frequently chooses company blogs or SEO-spam sites over authoritative sources

evidence_items.explanation: An independent evaluation of the launch version found that Deep Research often relied on SEO-spam and other weak sources. This supports "poorly-cited."

receipt.public_excerpt: Deep research in ChatGPT is currently very compute intensive.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI itself confirms that Deep Research used heavy compute. The same section admits it may struggle to tell authoritative sources from rumors.

unresolved_gaps: There is no independent, systematic measurement of Operator's real-world completion rate or of how long it takes compared with a person doing the same task.
The benchmark figures are OpenAI's own and were not independently replicated in the sources cited.
